maya: Hey - hitting a weird handshake failure when onboarding a Dedicated customer behind a corporate HTTP proxy + custom CA. Works with curl but our async sample app fails. stack trace: 

kevin: can you paste the minimal repro + env?

maya: repro summary: Dedicated base_url=https://dedicated-eu.redwood.local, proxy=http://corp-proxy:3128, custom CA at /etc/ssl/custom-root.pem. using the async client example from docs. error: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 42, in <module>
    await client.chat.completions.create(...)
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/httpx/_exceptions.py", line 244, in send
    raise SSLError("[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed") from exc
httpx._exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed
```

kevin: hmm. are you using the async httpx transport from our SDK? python version + httpx version?

maya: python 3.11, httpx 0.25.0, redwood-python 0.12.3 (pinned). the sync requests-based sample works when I set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/custom-root.pem but the async sample still fails.

liz: yes this rings a bell. httpx/asyncio needs an ssl.SSLContext passed to the AsyncClient or to the underlying httpcore transport. Our SDK currently forwards `verify` only for sync path but not always for async path in Dedicated mode when proxies are present.

samir: repro note: there's also a precedence bug — when you supply `proxies` or HTTP_PROXY environment, the SDK re-initializes a session and accidentally drops the `base_url` custom CA handling during the redirect to the proxy tunnel.

maya: ugh. any temporary workarounds other than switching to sync? customer can't change proxy config.

liz: two options now: 1) create an explicit SSLContext and pass via `client._httpx_client._transport` (ugly internal hack), or 2) set SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/custom-root.pem in the process env — httpx will read it if not overridden. Example quick hack:
```
import os
os.environ.setdefault("SSL_CERT_FILE", "/etc/ssl/custom-root.pem")
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(base_url="https://dedicated-eu.redwood.local", api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"]) 
```

kevin: adding to that — if you're using aiohttp directly you can do: 
```
import ssl
ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile="/etc/ssl/custom-root.pem")
connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ssl_ctx)
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=connector)
# then use httpx.AsyncClient(transport=httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(client=session))
```

samir: for the SDK fix: we should accept an explicit `trust_store`/`ssl_context` kwarg on AsyncClient and thread it into httpx transport creation. Also make sure proxy path preserves verify flags. This will be a small API addition and a behavior fix. CC @liz for PR.

liz: will do. I'll draft a PR that: 1) adds `ssl_context` and `ca_certs` params to AsyncClient/Client constructors 2) wires them into httpx transport for both sync and async paths 3) adds tests mocking an HTTPS proxy and custom CA 4) documents env var precedence (SSL_CERT_FILE, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, REDWOOD_CA_PATH)

maya: amazing, thx. can you add a short backwards-compatible shim so users who pass `verify` (bool/path) still work? we have production users depending on that param in older versions.

liz: yeah, plan is: if verify is bool True -> default; if str -> treat like cafile; if `ssl_context` provided -> prefer it. We'll add deprecation warning for verify=str in next minor.

kevin: also let's add typing stubs for these new params + overloads so IDEs surface them. People kept opening issues about confusing AsyncClient signature.

samir: small UX ask: add a troubleshooting snippet in the Dedicated onboarding doc with exact env var combos that are supported and examples for common proxy vendors (squid/bluecoat/windows proxy). That would save support calls.

maya: yes please. Also backstage note: customer reported base_url getting ignored if proxies are set and REDWOOD_BASE_URL env var is present vs passing base_url param; we should document precedence (param > env var > default).

deploy-bot: CI pipeline:redwood-python#3824 queued for build :gear:

kevin: thanks — liz, want me to pair-review the PR? happy to help with tests.

liz: appreciate it. I'll open draft PR and link here. will include a tiny sample app repo showing both sync and async patterns behind corporate proxy.

maya: awesome - that will unblock onboarding. :raised_hands:

samir: follow-up: let's add a short e2e test in infra that spins up a tiny mitmproxy container with a cert signed by a test CA so we catch regressions in CI.

kevin: good call.

maya: I'll keep this thread updated with customer status, thanks everyone.
